probe.question: Fragment DNA and introduce sequencing adapter sequences using adapter-loaded Tn5 transposase.

channels.query: Perform production-library nick translation. After tagmentation, add the reported FailSafe master mix, polymerase and water, then incubate for nick translation. This is the named repair transformation to an Illumina-ready library, not a production-library PCR programme. The packet does not resolve transposase release, exact strand replacement or residual nicks; no additional ligase or pre-repair cleanup operation is supplied. Fragment genomic DNA and join ME adaptors. React previously prepared genomic DNA with an aliquot of custom transposomes. Transposase activity couples fragmentation to end-joining of synthetic ME adaptor to target-DNA 5' ends, supplying the NoPCR adaptor domains on the genomic fragments.

Previously prepared genomic DNA, 100 or 200 ng per selected reaction. Published applicability is demonstrated for bacterial and human genomic DNA; DNA isolation is upstream of this scoped route. Ez-Tn5 transposase assembled with the custom annealed NoPCR adaptors in glycerol; prepared complexes supply the transposition reaction.
Unpurified NoPCR library reaction after the 72°C nick-translation incubation; the authors describe the product as Illumina-ready. No claim of complete covalent sealing of every strand is made.

Preserves genomic inserts and adaptor domains while effecting the reported repair needed for the Illumina-ready endpoint. Complete covalent sealing is not asserted. Retains genomic insert identity in fragmented adaptor-bearing molecules. The discussion limits control of insert-size distribution and notes high-G+C bias potentially correctable in part by the PCR-free approach; no universal insert size or bias-free output is established.

channels.query: Complete monitored production amplification. Apply the qPCR-determined additional cycles to the retained 45 μL production reaction using the reported production-PCR thermal cycle settings. Stop before saturation; the source reports 10–12 total library cycles, without making that range the universal controller. Monitor amplification and select cycles. Add 10 μL PCR cocktail to the analytical aliquot, with Sybr Green at final 0.6x; run this analytical reaction for 20 cycles. Use its qPCR readout to determine additional cycles for the retained 45 μL production reaction so amplification stops before saturation. Full analytical thermal program and quantitative decision criterion are unresolved. Remove analytical aliquot. Inputs are mutually exclusive alternatives: perform this split on one chosen standard or low-cell production reaction, never pool them. After five full-library cycles, physically remove an aliquot for analytical monitoring; retain the reported remaining 45 μL production reaction. The low-cell production PCR starts at the explicitly reported 50 μL; the standard starting production volume and explicit removed-aliquot amount are unspecified. Extension of monitoring to the low-cell branch follows the explicit same-protocol statement.

One standard-branch PCR reaction from Minelute-purified transposed DNA after five initial library cycles. Retains originating specimen/population and input-count branch; the original PCR-oligo names/sequences are available as an inventory, while the selected indexed oligo, its per-library assignment and complete fragment terminal structures remain unresolved. One conditional low-cell PCR reaction receiving the entire unpurified 5 μL transposition reaction into the reported 50 μL PCR after five initial library cycles. Retains originating specimen/population and input-count branch; the original PCR-oligo names/sequences are available as an inventory, while the selected indexed oligo, its per-library assignment and complete fragment terminal structures remain unresolved.

Retained production library after additional qPCR-selected cycles. Reported total 10–12 cycles is an outcome, not a fixed universal rule; analytical product is not included. Separately amplified analytical qPCR product after 20 cycles, with added PCR cocktail/Sybr Green. This branch terminates as analytical material; no return to production is supported.

probe.question: Preserve the origin of captured RNA through pooling by linking its identity to a molecular barcode.

channels.query: Reverse transcribe and template switch in bulk. Add 200 µL RT mix to a pellet of up to 90,000 recovered beads. Incubate 30 min at room temperature, then 90 min at 42 °C. Extend bead-attached oligo-dT from captured mRNA to stable covalent cDNA and introduce the downstream PCR handle by template switching. RT occurs after recovery, unlike the separate synRNA bead-validation experiment. Lyse and capture RNA within droplets. Immediately after compartmentalization, lyse cells in bead-supplied lysis buffer and hybridize released poly(A) mRNA to bead oligo-dT; the bumpy outlet promotes mixing. No additional lysis incubation or separately invented postmix recipe is assigned. Co-flow and partition cells with beads. Load separate cell/bead 3 mL syringes, with a 6.4 mm stir disc in the bead syringe, and oil in a 10 mL syringe. Pump each aqueous feed at 4.1 mL/hr and oil at 14 mL/hr through the original 125 µm device. Stir beads continuously and gently. Collect in 50 mL tubes, changing tubes after every 1 mL combined aqueous volume. Laminar flow keeps inputs separate before droplet formation; equal aqueous contributions give 60 beads/µL inside droplets from 120/µL feed. Break emulsion and recover the bead pellet. Immediately after generation, remove bottom oil with P1000, add 30 mL room-temperature 6X SSC and 600 µL perfluoro-1-octanol, shake approximately 20 s, then spin 1 min at 1000×g. Keep on ice for the remaining breakage protocol. Remove supernatant to roughly 5 mL above the interface, wash in another 30 mL room-temperature 6X SSC, transfer aqueous layer and re-pellet; second-spin settings are not separately specified. Transfer pellet to nonstick tubes, wash twice with 1 mL 6X SSC and once with 300 µL 5x Maxima H− RT buffer. Allocate an optional droplet inspection fraction. Optional implementation branch: remove a physical microscopy aliquot while retaining the production fraction; the inexpensive example places 3 µL droplets with 17 µL oil in a Fuchs-Rosenthal chamber. If omitted, pass the entire emulsion to recovery; no QC material returns to production.

Consumed stock aliquot resuspended at approximately 120 beads/µL in DLB + 50 mM DTT; this is the syringe concentration. Supplied intact single-cell suspension. Specimen-specific dissociation/culture is outside the general interface. Carrier and concentration are qualified choices, rather than a universal viability gate or historical retina reconstruction.

Bulk-RT bead-associated cDNA STAMPs: extended capture primers covalently retain their bead-linked 5′ constant handle, cell barcode and UMI; template switching has introduced the second PCR handle downstream of cDNA. Optional removed droplet aliquot for microscopy, physically distinct from the retained production emulsion. The low-cost implementation example uses 3 µL droplets with 17 µL oil.

Stabilizes the captured transcript’s association with the original cell-barcode/UMI primer and supplies the opposite amplification handle. Associates a cell lysate with its companion bead before pooling; the barcode initially identifies a bead, with cell association contingent on occupancy. Spatial isolation makes bead barcode a potential cell-associated origin tag, subject to occupancy and ambient-RNA limitations. Large aqueous dilution reduces postbreakage hybridization; subsequent cold handling reduces RNA dissociation, preserving the prior bead assignment rather than establishing new cell isolation. Creates an analytical fraction, not a duplicate of the production emulsion.
